To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the BV generated by cloud computing is not affected by firm's human capital (general and ICT human capital), (2) the co-operation between ICT and business units is not a significant determinant of the BV generated by the cloud, (3) there is a positive effect of the relationship between ICT and business unit's personnel on the cloud BV, (4) there is a negative effect of the relationship with the business units' personnel on the BV generated from cloud computing.
the BV generated by cloud computing is positively affected by the co-operation and the relationship between the personnel in the ICT unit and that of the business units.
the BV of CC is positively affected by the co-operation and the relationships of the ICT unit personnel with the business units' personnel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the human determinants of CC business value, in order to provide a more complete and holistic view of CC BV.

the investigation of the human factors, which impact the BV generated from CC and the results are expected to contribute to a better understanding of the CC business value and the human factors that impact its realization, which can be of great interest for firms and policy makers, who wish to adopt CC.

the investigation of the effect of a specific type of human capital, i.e. ICT human capital, and of a specific type and level of co-operation between the personnel of two different departments of a firm, i.e. the ICT unit and business units, on CC BV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the BV generated by cloud computing is positively impacted by a set of factors that concern the human capital of the ICT unit of the firm, as well as by the relationship between the ICT and the business unit.
the BV generated by firms from CC is mainly determined by the ICT personnel's co-operation with the business unit personnel.
CC can generate sizeable BV for firms only if it is supported by a high quality of the co-operation between the personnel of its ICT and its business units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, although the BV generated by cloud computing is not directly affected by human capital per se, it is affected by human capital, insofar as it is used in a way that enhances the co-operation and the relationship among the employees of the ICT unit with those of the business units.
CC is a business value generating tool for firms, but it is not a'silver bullet'.

the BV generated by the adoption and implementation of CC is mainly determined by the ICT personnel of the firm, who are responsible for the CC adoption, as well as by the business personnel who are responsible for its utilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the co-operation and the relationship between the personnel in the ICT units and the personnel in the business units, which are the most crucial elements in the successful implementation of CC, have a positive and significant impact on the BV generated from CC.

the co-operation between the personnel of ICT unit and the business units of the firm is a key determinant for the generation of BV by CC, as it is quantified by the share (percentage) of the ICT unit employees that are assigned to business units, in order to provide them with the necessary IT support.
the BV generated by firms from CC depends on the co-operation between the ICT and business personnel, which is quantified by the co-ordination and communication between the two groups of personnel.
